A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 54-page FormulaCode study, including Appendices A and B. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish complete comparability; differences are confined to publication labeling and PDF title metadata.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original evaluations of seven agent/model configurations on 108 FormulaCode-V tasks. Appendix B includes additional quantitative analyses and human-versus-agent patch case studies.

after.justification: The same original evaluations, numerical results, and appendix analyses remain in v2, including Table 1 and Appendices B.3–B.4.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, environment-synthesis agent, correctness checks, and evaluation harness in Section 2 and Appendices A–B are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same reported 957 tasks across 70 repositories and the 108-task FormulaCode-V evaluation subset. No datasets, task requirements, or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same seven Terminus 2/OpenHands configurations involving GPT-5, Claude 4.0 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Qwen 3 Coder, alongside the human-expert reference. Comparator membership also matches within the supplementary comparisons.

E3.justification: The evaluation subset, metrics, correctness-based rollback rules, ASV measurement procedures, and sequential evaluation in fresh containers remain unchanged (Sections 2.1, B.1.6, and B.2.5).

E4.justification: The optimization-scope, optimization-type, popularity, cost, and temporal analyses in Section 3 are identical. Appendices B.3–B.4 retain the same correctness, trajectory, tool-use, and patch case studies.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1.6 retains the same repeated-measurement procedure, Mann–Whitney U threshold of p < 0.002, and fallback using non-overlapping 99% confidence intervals. No run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains OpenHands with Claude 4.0 Sonnet at RP rank 1 with advantage -0.0112; appendix result tables and patch case studies are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of speedup and the advantage metrics in Section 2.1, together with the statistical formulation in Appendix B.1.6, are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution of a live benchmark for repository-level, multi-workload optimization and the same claims about agents' performance relative to human experts.

C2.justification: Interpretations of optimization scope, repository popularity, cost tradeoffs, temporal leakage, and agent failures are unchanged. The same compute-related scope restrictions and benchmark limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation details, build prompts, model identifiers, hardware specifications, environment setup, resource requirements, and project access disclosures remain unchanged, including those in Appendix B.

R1.justification: Section 4, Table 5, and the reference list are identical. No cited works or substantive positioning relative to earlier benchmarks and optimization methods change.

P1.justification: Body text, the printed title, and document structure are unchanged. The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 16 March 2026 to v2 dated 14 May 2026, and PDF title metadata adds 'FormulaCode:', already present in both printed titles.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and page layout are unchanged throughout the main paper and appendices. Rendered pages 2–54 match exactly; page 1 differs only in the margin stamp text.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, Table 1 results, appendix analyses, explanations, and reproducibility information are unchanged. Updating the arXiv label and aligning PDF title metadata with the existing printed title does not materially improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
